startup.name: Pennant
startup.one_liner: The World Model for Corporate Governance
startup.description: Pennant builds voting and governance intelligence for institutional investors, public companies and corporate advisors, so that they can vote and engage according to their own principles at scale. It is led by two former institutional proxy voters and technologists. Buyers are asset managers, issuers and advisors who currently pay proxy advisors and data vendors. Two founders in New York.

yc_acceptance.basis: In this test the company is assumed accepted to YC for Summer 2026. Prior is about 1 percent. Strong domain expertise (20 plus years) raises the odds, but the market is narrow, there is no stated traction and only two people. About 2.5 percent.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly pass because proxy voting is a small, regulated market dominated by two firms, sales to asset managers are slow, and partners may doubt whether the revenue pool supports a venture scale company.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The company fails to reach a meaningful exit if proxy voting remains a small concentrated market, if large asset managers build their own AI voting, or if ISS and Glass Lewis add equivalent features with their data advantage and customer relationships.

technical_complexity.rationale: Parsing filings, policies and votes with language models is feasible for a small team, but accuracy on nuanced global governance issues is hard and incumbents have years of data. Domain expertise is the moat.

who: in house teams at big asset managers
takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents are adding AI features and have customers, though their slow pace and regulatory pressure give a window.

Regulatory pressure on proxy advisors is creating openings for alternatives.

brand.name: Pennant
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Pennant" --era 2022+ : 7 characters, 2 syllables, real word
brand.strengths: Real word, easy to say, suggests a flag or a position
brand.weaknesses: Does not say governance, shared with other brands
brand.rationale: The name is a real word that fits finance and signalling, easy to say and remember. It does not describe the product, but buyers choose institutional tools by trust, so the effect is small.

narrative.headline: Credible domain founders in a narrow, concentrated market, so a seed is a coin flip and later rounds are hard.
narrative.general_summary: Pennant pairs former proxy voters with AI to serve a market dominated by ISS and Glass Lewis, where customers are moving toward customized and AI assisted voting. The domain expertise is a real strength. The market is small, sales cycles are slow, and big asset managers are building their own tools. A seed above the YC check is about a coin flip and later steps sit slightly below the cohort anchors. The upside path is a pivot to a broader governance data product for issuers and advisors. Reaching a round years later is common for companies with paying customers.

assumptions: Test is blind: only the YC input file was used for company facts.
Seed means a round above $500K within about 12 months.
Fintech cohort has only 26 companies, so B2B figures were used too.
